description.en:
"Feeling a bit nervous?" Truth noticed Olga's hand trembling slightly.
"Afraid the smell of new wood will bother the kids?" she teased.
Olga chuckled softly. "As if. I'd be thankful if those kids didn't doodle all over the desks." She looked up at the quiet house before her, and added, "Just didn't expect it to be so quiet here. I am a bit nervous though... Don't make fun of me."
"First day, being nervous is normal." Truth paced back and forth a few times, looking at the books and documents in Olga's hand. "Sure you don't want to put them in the library, maybe even put a glass case over them? At least it'd have some commemorative value."
The Tripolov family's ancestral home was empty. After removing the grandiose furnishings, it looked like nothing more than an empty house. It appeared exceptionally quiet, awaiting someone's arrival. Pushing open the unlocked door, Olga and Truth walked through the rooms and connecting corridors, finally arriving at the lawn in front of the door. They sat down, placing the books and documents they held onto the lawn. Morning mist lingered, the grass was damp, and the paper was moistened by the dew on the grass leaves, leaving marks on the page corners.
"...I told you not to make fun of me." Olga flipped through a few pages of paper. "These are all things from before. Sketchbooks from when I was a kid, scripts written in practice class... Put these in a glass case? I'm afraid they, just like this agreement, can't provide any useful help to the children."
She stood up and walked a few steps toward the piano in the center of the lawn. "Perhaps the only useful thing is this sheet music."
"I remember you compose your own music," Truth said, "haven't played it for me yet." She looked at Olga. "Didn't you think it was too quiet here? Then... right now? Five minutes before the official start of school."
When the first batch of students from the academy walked through the iron gates into the Petrashevsky campus, this was the tune they heard. The sound of the piano replaced the school bell to welcome these children, and many fresh faces full of vitality clustered around, gathering by Olga's side. A girl mustered up the courage to take a step forward, but shyly covered the patch on her sleeve. She timidly asked Olga: "Hello... May I ask what this song is called?"
What is it called? Olga thought. It was just a casual little tune. Written during the most difficult times, written late at night while bent over work, written under two dim candles. It had no name, and even today was the first time Olga had played it.
Olga paused for a moment, smiled, took the girl's hand covering the patch, and gently moved it away—that was a rough, warm hand with light calluses.
"It has no name. It's just a song from yesterday."
description.zh:
“有点紧张？”真理察觉到奥尔佳的手微微发抖。
“怕那些新木头的味道熏到孩子们？”她揶揄道。
奥尔佳轻笑一声。“怎么可能。那些孩子不在桌子上涂涂画画就谢天谢地了。”她抬头望向眼前沉静的房屋，又补充了一句，“只是没想到这里这么安静，紧张倒还真有一点……你别打趣我。”
“第一天，紧张很正常。”真理原地踱了几步，看向奥尔佳手中拿着的书和文件，“确定不放在图书室里，也拿个玻璃罩子罩起来？也算有点纪念意义。”
特里波列夫家的祖宅已经空了。挪走辉煌的陈设后，这里看上去只是一栋空旷的房子而已。它显得格外安静，正等待着什么人的到来。推开没有锁的门，奥尔佳和真理穿过屋室与连廊，最终走到了门前的草坪上。她们坐下来，将手中的书本与文件放在了草坪上。清晨薄雾弥漫，青草湿润，纸张被草叶上的露珠打湿，页角留下痕迹。
“……都说让你别打趣我了。”奥尔佳翻开几页纸，“这都是之前的东西。小时候的素描本、习作课上写的剧本……把这些东西放进玻璃罩子里？恐怕它们和这份协议一样，没办法给孩子们提供任何有用的帮助。”
她站起身，往草坪中央的钢琴旁走了几步。“可能唯一有用的，就是这本琴谱了。”
“我记得你会自己作曲，”真理说，“还没给我听过。”她看向奥尔佳，“你不是嫌这里太安静了吗，那……就现在？离正式开学还有五分钟。”
当学院的第一批学生从铁门走进彼得拉设夫斯基校舍时，听到的就是这支曲子。琴声代替了开学的铃声来欢迎这些孩子，许多带着生气的新鲜面孔簇过来，聚集在奥尔佳的身旁。一个女孩鼓起勇气向前走了一步，却赧然地遮掩起自己袖口的补丁。她怯生生地向奥尔佳提问：“您好……想请问这首曲子，叫什么名字？”
它叫什么名字？奥尔佳想。它只是一首随手写下的小调。写于最艰难的时候，写于某个伏案工作的深夜，写于两盏微弱的烛火之下。它没有名字，甚至在今天，奥尔佳才第一次弹奏它。
奥尔佳沉吟片刻，她微笑，握住女孩掩在补丁上的手，将它轻柔地从补丁上挪开——那是一只粗糙、温暖，带有薄茧的手。
“它没有名字。它只是一首来自昨天的歌。”
